styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Bow River paths, Fish Creek Park and a day in the Rockies.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Glenbow-style museums, the Stampede story and Inglewood's old streets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Steak, brunch and a growing craft-beer scene.

stays.why: Walk to the CTrain on 7th Avenue, the Calgary Tower and the Bow River paths. Best base without a car.
Just south of downtown: most restaurants and bars per block, still walkable to the core.
Quiet, leafy and close to the river and Prince's Island Park; good for walks and cafés.
Oldest neighbourhood: independent shops, breweries and the river; short bus ride to downtown.

food: Try Alberta beef at least once: steakhouses downtown and in the Beltline, roughly CAD 35–70 for a main.
Brunch is a local habit. Expect lineups on weekend mornings; go before 10am or book ahead.
Local craft beer is easy to find: taprooms in the Beltline and Inglewood, about CAD 8–10 a pint.
Cheap eats: Vietnamese, Korean and donair shops in the Beltline and Forest Lawn, about CAD 12–20 a meal.
The Calgary Farmers' Market is good for local produce and snacks; check opening days on the day.
more_time: Add a day in the Rockies: Banff is about 1.5 hours west by car or bus. Check road and park pass details before you go.
Dinosaur fans can swap a city afternoon for Drumheller and the Royal Tyrrell Museum, about 1.5 hours east by car.
In July, give the Calgary Stampede a full day or evening rather than squeezing it in.

recommend.why: Two nights covers downtown, the river paths and one Rockies day; add a third night for Drumheller or the Stampede.

month_notes: January: cold, highs near -2°C and lows around -12°C. Dress in layers and watch for ice.
February: still cold, about -2°C high and -13°C low, with the most snow days of winter. Warm boots help.
March: slowly warming, highs near 4°C but nights still below freezing. Expect slush.
April: highs around 10°C, lows near -2°C. Mild days mix with cold snaps; pack a warm layer.
May: pleasant at about 17°C, but the wettest-ish month with around 10 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
June: mild at about 21°C with around 13 rain days. Showers pass quickly; evenings are cool.
July: warmest month, highs near 24°C and lows around 11°C. Stampede time; book hotels early.
August: warm and similar to July, about 23°C high. Good for parks and day trips.
September: comfortable at about 18°C, fewer rain days. A strong month for walking and the Rockies.
October: cooling to about 11°C, nights near 0°C. First frosts possible; bring a jacket.
November: cold again, highs near 3°C and lows around -7°C. Short days; plan indoor sights.
December: cold, about -3°C high and -12°C low. Snow possible; check conditions before driving.

climate_guide.summary: Cold, dry winters and short, mild summers. Rain is spread through the year, heaviest in June.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Highs of 18–24°C and long days. Ideal for the river paths, parks and Rockies day trips.

items.title: Winter is genuinely cold
items.text: December to February highs sit near -2 to -3°C, with lows around -12°C. Pack a real coat, hat and gloves.

items.title: Rain peaks in June
items.text: About 13 rain days in June, versus 4–8 in most other months. Showers are usually short.

items.title: Spring and fall swing widely
items.text: April and October can be mild one day and cold the next. Layers beat a single heavy outfit.

items.title: Snow is possible in winter
items.text: February has the most snow days in the averages. Watch for icy sidewalks and check road conditions.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Summer: light layers and a rain jacket. Winter: insulated coat, boots, hat and gloves. Always bring a warm layer for evenings.

transit.best: CTrain for downtown and nearby stops; walk the compact core and use buses or ride apps for the rest.

modes.text: CTrain light rail runs two lines, Red and Blue, through downtown on 7th Avenue South, which is transit-only.
Calgary Transit buses fill the gaps. A single fare is about $4 adult, $2.65 youth, free for ages 12 and under.
Taxis are metered. Uber is the main ride-hailing app and the only one authorized at the airport.
Driving is easy outside rush hour. Downtown parking is expensive, so use park-and-ride at suburban stations.
Downtown is compact and walkable. The Bow River pathways are good for bikes and rentals.
No ferries; the city is inland.
